paragraphs.text: Dear sisters and elders, another day in paradise. Hope you made it great through your hard choices. Remember hard choices now make for an easy and productive life later. Easy choices now rob you of the amazing future you could have had.

You build your life one choice at a time. Each great decision that you act on leads to more skill and more knowledge which leads you to more opportunities and a super high quality life. Remember remember it's your choice.

No new updates for today but I'm very hopeful that President Duterte will announce a more flexible lockdown when he makes his announcement to the nation on Thursday. Let's keep hoping and praying for that.

Now let's talk about smooth stones that can help you win the battles against the Goliaths in your life. Smooth stone number three is all about building predictability to your life. You do that by using processes and systems.

After World War II Japan was completely destroyed. The Allied forces had bombed all the factories and from what I've read there was nothing still standing in that country bigger than a one-story building and there weren't very many of those. It was utter devastation.

How are the Japanese going to get back on their feet and build an economy that could feed their people? It was a monumental job and many people couldn't see how it could ever be done and certainly not in less than 30 or 40 years.

But there was a man named W. Edward Deming who was an expert at building processes and systems. The United States sent Deming over to Japan and he worked with the Japanese government and business leaders and within 10 years Japan was bigger and stronger as a manufacturer and a business economy than it ever had been before.

Later on Deming wrote a few books about what he did and what he learned. One statement that he said has been a part of my thinking ever since I read it. Deming said this quote, "if you can't describe what you're doing as a process then you really don't know what you're doing."

What he meant by that is pretty simple really. He wanted everyone to understand that to really know how to do something in a productive and predictable consistent way you have to be able to break it down into steps.

You need to know what comes first and what comes second and so forth until you have the thing you want finished and done. Some people can do something but they don't really know how they do it. Deming would say that they're only half way to knowing it because they can't actually describe their process and therefore they can't teach anyone else how to do it.

A process is really nothing more than a series of steps that can be repeated again and again and will produce the same result again and again. A system is simply a collection of these processes that fit together to bring about an even more complex result.

Now you might think about this in connection with your health. There are several aspects to good health. What you eat is one, how you exercise is another, how you sleep is another, how you handle stress is another, how you practice hygiene is another and we could go on and on.

Each of these separate parts of health, if you were going to focus on this mindset that we're talking about of smooth stone number three, each of these separate parts would have its own process to maximize the outcome.

For instance with regard to what you eat you would want to discover what are the big levers to maximizing a great diet. What are the few things that will produce the most benefit? Kind of in thinking of what we talked about yesterday, the 80-20 principle.

Now there are millions of books written about diets but there are just a few key levers that actually make up most of the benefit of a healthy diet and if you do those few you will get most of the benefits. You don't need to read all those books, you just need to do those few.

And as we talked about yesterday when we deal with the 80-20 the 20 is always the hard stuff. When we break it down to the 4% it's even harder. When we break it down to the 1% it's really hard but those really hard things produce the maximum benefit for your efforts doing them.

You do the same thing with exercise. Here again there's millions of books written on exercise but there's really only a few things that make all the difference in exercise. Same thing with sleep, stress, hygiene, etc. In other words you build a process for each one of those parts and by so doing you have in fact built a system for your health.

You use process to build systems using systems to build a really high quality life. Now this next concept that I want to share with you is one that a lot of people don't like to hear but it's true so you need to know it.
The great Japanese swordsman Miyamoto Musashi said quote, "truth is not what you want it to be it is what it is and you must bend to its power or live a lie."

And I would add not only will you live a lie but you will die of failure unless you learn the truth and deal with it well whether you like it or not. It's key. So here is the truth that a lot of people don't like and they don't like it because everybody kind of wants to do their own thing and the scriptures we read every man walketh in his own way.

Well the truth is this there is one best way to do anything at any given period of time and in any place. You must find that way for your thing in your time and in your place and it's not easy but there's a process for doing it and the process also came from Deming. It's called PDCA.

P for plan it out. D for do it according to your plan. C for check the results and measure them against your goals. A is for act to modify your plan and refine it if necessary and then start the cycle over again, PDCA.

As you do this again and again you build a proven process that is both documented and duplicatable by a normal average person. Once you have this kind of process, once you've refined it to this level of structure and simplicity, once you've validated it multiple times, then you have created a part of a system.

As you do that with other processes working to that same end you create a complete system built on these proven documented processes. Now with a system you can create leverage in your life and in your business enterprise and in the missionary work. In fact we do this in our missionary work.

You can also create consistency and predictability. One of the reasons the Cagayan de Oro Mission has been so consistent over the months is that we operate on process and systems and that's what gives us consistency even though we have this constant flow of new missionaries coming in and seasoned experienced missionaries going home.

Nothing is really big that nothing is there's nothing great elders and sisters that is created without leverage. Nobody's got enough time or enough skill to do everything. Real estate investors know this. They have to use other people's money in order to buy lots of real estate and then hope it goes up.

The problem with real estate leverage is if what you buy with other people's money goes down now you don't even have an asset to pay off the debt that you took upon yourself. It can be incredibly destructive that way. However system leverage is very different. It's the ultimate win-win leverage.

In fact it's the only kind of leverage I've ever seen that doesn't have a downside. It's only positive. With system leverage you're in effect leveraging your knowledge, your time, and your processes to an infinite level.

Let me give you an example. You have your developed system that you've built over time and you've got all the processes refined and documented. Now you can hire an average normal person to use your process to do that part of your business.
You'll need to monitor and manage them for a little while but eventually they'll get it and can do it very well beyond their natural ability because they're using your proven process.

Now while you're delegating this part of your business or your work to the system and to the employee you now have, you can now use that time to build another process or to build another system for another aspect of your life that you want to build out.

And this can go on and on until you get tired of growing which you should never do because there's always new mountains to climb and new goals to achieve. We believe in eternal progression and so why not get started now?

As you think about this and this is going to take I think most of you are going to need to listen to this a few times to grasp the concept but I want you to make it simple and you can do that with your own health. Build a system for diet.

Figure out what the three or four things are that make all the difference in having a healthy diet. Then build a system for exercise. You don't need to be an Olympic athlete exercising. You just need to do the three or four things that create the optimal benefits and maximize the greatest results in the time that you have.

Now you've got a process for diet and you've got a process for exercise and you can look at a process for how you get the best sleep. When you go to sleep what you do before you're asleep and so forth.

I mean a couple of things when I first got the mission, people would tell me missionaries would say, brother I can't get any sleep at night. I just lay in bed. I can't sleep. I don't know what to do. They don't even sleep till one o'clock and I said what time is your dinner meal?

When we get in from working about 9:30. I says there's your problem. You just put fuel in the tank and you expect to go to sleep. Your body just took on fuel. It thinks you're going to go do something.

If you eat at five or six and then go to sleep at 9:30 or 10, your body's ready for sleep. But if you eat at 9:30 or 10 o'clock, you're not going to get to sleep until about one o'clock or you're going to have a really bad night's sleep. Other things you can do.

A cold shower before sleep really, really maximizes your sleep and there's a few other things that you can do. Don't look at the smartphone for an hour and a half before you go to sleep because the blue light coming off the smartphone messes up your melatonin and your melatonin is what allows you to go to sleep.

So you can figure all these things out, elders and sisters, and you can build a process for sleep. You can build a process for stress. It's right there to adjusting to missionary life. You can build a process for your diet as we talked about. You can build a process for your hygiene.

You know when do I brush? Do I rinse? When do I floss? You know what kind of shower do I take? You know when all these things are processes and if you build processes you don't have to be making these decisions all the time. Should I do that today? Should I do it now? Should I do it later?

You got a process. You get up, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom. Now some people have said to me, man it's like being like a machine. I don't want to be that way. I want to be spontaneous. I want to just do my thing.

And my answer is you're never going to do much of anything because you're too busy making decisions about what you're going to do right now. Whereas I got processes and I just crank those things out which leaves me free time to go do the things I really enjoy doing without having to worry about the things I didn't do because I did do them.

So anyway, think about this, ponder it, re-listen to this, and start building some processes into your missionary life. Start creating five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten step processes for every important thing that you want to do to maximize your mission.
And when you get done with your mission you'll have a powerful system of how to be an awesome missionary. A highly productive, consistently predictable, effective missionary.

Now you sit down with these other people who are getting ready to go on their mission and you say let me show you my system for being amazing as a missionary. It's broken into these six processes. And when I do these six processes I produce an amazing outcome and so will you young man or young woman.

Can you see the value of that? Because not only have you had the experience, now you can teach others how to have a great experience because you built the processes, you've created the system, and you've documented it and now it's yours.

And you can do that same thing in what kind of a student you're going to be, the same thing on what kind of lawyer or doctor or architect or whatever job you want you're going to be, you can build a process into that, you can build a process in what kind of a family you're going to have.

All those things, quite frankly, are important enough that you ought to build processes and systems around them. God bless you all. Hope you have a great night tonight. Talk to you again tomorrow and I hope you know we love you.
